title: react: `useClientNotifications` ships a polling notification bridge with zero call sites — dead, and a live second-scheduler trap next to the shared inbox feed
body:
Ruled: 5809224666 · letter remove · 2026-09-24T06:51Z

## What

`packages/react/src/hooks/useClientNotifications.ts` exports a notification
bridge hook that owns its own poller:

```
packages/react/src/hooks/useClientNotifications.ts:198
    const id = setInterval(() => { ... }, pollInterval);
```

It is exported from the package barrel (`packages/react/src/hooks/index.ts:29`)
and **has zero call sites in this repo**. Every mention outside its own file is
the barrel line, `content/docs/guide/notifications.md:224`, and two
`packages/react/CHANGELOG.md` entries — no component or app mounts it.

## Why it is worth recording rather than leaving

Two things, and the second is the reason this is filed at all:

1. **Dead surface.** It is published API that nothing consumes, carrying a
   `fetchNotifications` / `markAsRead` implementation against
   `client.notifications.*` that no test exercises through a real mount.

2. **It is the exact hazard the inbox-cadence work exists to prevent.** The
   console's user-scoped feeds were deliberately consolidated onto one shared
   scheduler (`packages/app-shell/src/hooks/sharedUserFeeds.ts`) across
   objectui#4197 / #4225 / #4316, so the bell and Home's action centre cannot
   issue two reads or disagree about read-state. `useClientNotifications` is a
   second, independent poller over the same ADR-0030 notification rows, one
   import away from any consumer, writing into `NotificationContext` instead of
   the shared feed. Wiring it — which its docs page actively invites — would
   reintroduce precisely the duplicate-scheduler shape those three issues closed,
   and it would not be caught by the shared feed's own pins.

Found while investigating objectui#7249, which named this hook as a suspect for a
second scheduler on the console home page. It was NOT the cause there (it is not
mounted anywhere, so it polls nothing today) — that card's headline defect did not
reproduce; see PR #7387 for the measurements. This is the residue: the trap is
real even though it was not the culprit.

## Suggested dispositions (not a decision — for triage)

- Remove it (with a changeset and the docs section), if the notification bridge
  is not a supported extension point; or
- keep it but point it at the shared feed rather than its own `setInterval`, so
  there is one scheduler for these rows by construction; or
- keep it as-is and say so on the declaration, with the docs page warning that
  mounting it alongside the console shell duplicates the inbox read.

No assignee — recording only.
